method: Built-in imagegen: actual vessels, advanced tendinosis and rupture clefts painted into the anatomy bitmap; clinician source coordinates registered through native SVG
prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational, precise-object-edit / style-transfer.
Create the corrected PAINTED ANATOMY BITMAP for the Kansei Achilles viewer. The clinician has now explicitly identified all pathology. These changes MUST EXIST IN THE PAINTING ITSELF, without any annotation overlay.
IMAGE 1 is the edit target and established tissue-painting style. IMAGE 2 is the clinician's exact spatial guide and pathology key. IMAGE 3 is the original ultrasound and coordinate authority.
Keep the full 4:3 canvas, exactly the same framing, entire Achilles silhouette, golden lobulated Kager fat, warm trabecular calcaneus and original outer machine UI. Do not move or resize tissues. Keep the same rich natural ivory collagen, golden lobular fat and warm honeycomb bone painting; do not switch to cartoon, flat vector or schematic.
Interpret the guide as follows, then REMOVE ALL GUIDE INK:
BLUE encloses the entire thick Achilles tendon, including its upper-right portion and lower-left projection. Keep this full outline.
YELLOW short marks indicate NEOVASCULARISATION. Replace them with actual small branching blood vessels woven BETWEEN AND WITHIN the collagen fascicles across the left and middle tendon: roughly original x125..875, y225..390. Depict numerous delicate irregular tapering capillary/venular branches in natural muted red/burgundy, with tiny lumen/wall shading and subtle dimensional highlights, mostly 1.5–3 original pixels wide, often short branching segments. These must look like embedded biological vessels, not yellow lines, not flat red marker strokes, not a large artery tree laid on top. The capillaries must be clearly present with all labels and finding overlays turned OFF.
RED outer region marks a focal area of MORE ADVANCED TENDINOSIS WITHIN THE SAME TENDON at upper right. Original coordinates approx: starts at (893,188), follows upper tendon to (1028,175), then (1172,280), down to (1172,352), with lower margin through (1085,346),(1010,331),(930,312),(880,298), and irregular left edge near x875..905. In this region collagen must be visibly more disorganized, irregularly separated, heterogeneous and less parallel, with mottled warm grey/beige matrix. It must visibly differ from surrounding tendon texture, without a red-colored flood fill or a hard artificial tissue boundary.
PURPLE encloses genuine RUPTURE AREAS confirmed by the clinician. Depict clearly visible focal dark slate/blue-grey clefts with interrupted and frayed ivory collagen ends, irregular edges and subtle depth, within EXACTLY the purple shapes:
- two separate irregular branching/elongated rupture areas in the lower-middle tendon around x361..497,y363..417 and x392..497,y426..463;
- several small irregular rupture clefts WITHIN the advanced-tendinosis region at upper right: crescent at x961..995,y207..238; horizontal branching cleft x936..1002,y262..283; narrow oblique cleft x1045..1113,y228..280; irregular connected clefts x1060..1169,y284..355.
Keep these modest areas in their guide positions, not a complete transverse tendon transection and not a new large hole. The fibrous tissue must visibly break/part around each cleft, so these are readable actual tissue changes, NOT purple outlines painted on intact fibers.
GREEN encloses the existing TWO SMALL CHALKY CALCIFICATIONS near (944,345) and (1015,366). Retain their small sizes and chalky ivory texture.
Do not turn the red guide area into muscle or fat. Do not confuse rupture cavities with calcifications. Do not introduce another tendon, bursa, giant vessels, whole-tendon rupture or unrelated pathology. NO labels, arrows, outlines, dotted lines, yellow strokes, purple ink or red boundary ink anywhere in the final image. The result must be a coherent painted tissue scene in the original geometry, with natural small blood vessels, disrupted collagen and the focal degeneration all physically rendered.
